auditScope.title: Mark I records 448 through 687 individual physics-scope review
auditScope.includedRecordRange: Every numbered Mark I record 448-687 inclusive was reviewed individually. Record 454 contributes one new in-scope gap fact; records 533-537 were already cataloged by mark-i.json; every other record is enumerated below as a scoped exclusion or duplicate-evidence disposition.
auditScope.authorityBoundary: Only Algorithm32 physics, frozen CPU Reference realization or validation, and shader conformance to an exact pinned CPU Reference are fact scope. Renderer, browser, scene-light, endpoint-material, antialiasing, camera, image, stack-composition, and subjective gallery mechanics are excluded. A GPU-only or display-byte result cannot establish physics or shader-to-Reference conformance.
auditScope.lineageRule: The completed Mark I code identity remains commit cf3e00afbec1e81da66a062642dc233c32b54194 and scripts/flat/reconciliation/POC tree e5dbe65ed75fd0cd5ad144adadad3bc306d2f68c. Current working-tree POC bytes must not substitute. The missing record-414 bundle remains an explicit log-only provenance gap rather than being silently erased.

explicitExclusions.reason: Already reviewed and cataloged by mark-i.json; this remainder audit does not duplicate their cache, geometry, or unpinned selected-pixel facts and experiments.
Artifact-only interrupted placeholders with no result, criteria, or reviewable Algorithm32 claim bundle; retained as archive membership, not promoted as facts or experiments.

Rejected execution attempts. Their accepted criteria are setup or partial renderer observations, while the record-level result is rejected; they establish neither a Reference validation result nor shader conformance.

CPU and GPU display-image component runs consumed by record 454. Their constructed-scene, browser, hit-mask, and image-write mechanics are not separate physics facts; the comparison's authority defect and bounded numeric result are cataloged once through record 454.

Accepted phase-stack and review-stack assembly records preserve and label already-rendered display pixels. Image concatenation, labels, dimensions, and row order are presentation mechanics and add no Algorithm32 physics or pre-display Reference evidence.

Accepted browser-integrated CPU local/flat gallery runs repeat already-cataloged finite-hit, no-hit, endpoint-composition, flat/local input, and cache-participation observations. Their changing cameras, endpoint RGB proxies, ground materials, lights, shadows, boxes, dates, antialiasing, and display pixels are renderer/review policy; self-generated positive outputs do not add independent physics validation.

Accepted M4 GPU local/flat gallery records vary renderer distance/depth, endpoint fills, lighting, shadows, cameras, review objects, and display resolution. They perform no numeric comparison to an exact pinned CPU Reference. Their GPU-ideal/reference language and unpinned evidence defect are already owned by mark-i:m3:gpu-quality-comparison-uses-gpu-oracle, mark-i:m4:integrated-selected-pixel-result-not-conformance, and CONTRADICTION-A32-000022; no duplicate facts are created.

Accepted M4 GPU spherical/distant gallery records vary clocks, phase, endpoint scale, scene objects, shadow regions, fill, lighting, and display resolution. They retain renderer and GPU-image observations but no exact CPU Reference identity, input packet, pre-display comparison, or independent criterion. The existing GPU-oracle gap and CONTRADICTION-A32-000022 own that defect; these records do not become shader-conformance facts.
